title: Japan's Longest Loop Trail Opens in Ibaraki
paragraphs: Japan is famous for its big cities. But a new walking trail gives people a look into a very different side of the country.
The Hitachinokuni Long Trail, in Ibaraki Prefecture, is now open. And at 350 kilometers, it is Japan's longest loop trail.

The trail connects the cities of Kitaibaraki, Takahagi, Hitachi, Hitachiota and Hitachiomiya, as well as the town of Daigo. It takes walkers through mountains, villages, rice fields and beaches. And it's less than two hours from Tokyo by train!
Each part of the trail is different, so people can choose what they want to see and how difficult they want the walk to be. And because it doesn't get much snow in winter, it can be enjoyed all year.

Work on the trail began in 2019, and volunteers helped with much of it. The trail was officially opened on September 19 this year, after the last 75-kilometer part between Daigo and Hitachiomiya was finished.
But the trail was popular before it opened. In 2025, the Japan Long Trail Association asked people which of its 29 trails they most wanted to walk, and the Hitachinokuni Long Trail came first!
So for people looking to see a quieter side of Japan, the trail is waiting!
